Class Dock

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.swing.docking.Dock
@WindowScoped public final class Dock extends Object
The dock of a frame: views docked in it, split and tabbed, which the user rearranges, opened and closed while the frame is open, their layout saved with the frame's window state. A frame holds one dock, which its frame view, or any bean of the frame's window scope, injects; the frame view places its area(Consumer). Every method is called on the EDT.

  • Method Details

    • area

      public JComponent area(Consumer<? super Dock> layOut)
      Returns the dock's area, which the frame view returns from content() or places in it. It is called once, during the build of the frame view. Once that build has ended and its accessibility checks have run, before the frame is packed, the dock restores its saved layout; when there is none, or none of it can be restored, it calls layOut with itself, which opens the views of the frame's first layout. An empty dock shows an empty area.
      Parameters:
      layOut - opens the views of the first layout
      Returns:
      the area
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if called again, outside the build of a frame view, or in a dialog's window
      NullPointerException - if layOut is null

    • open

      public <V extends DockView> V open(Class<V> type, Placement placement)
      Opens a view of a dock view class, resolved through its child injector, and docks it as placement says. A dock holds at most one view of a class opened this way: when one is open, this brings it to the front, as toFront(DockView) does, ignores placement, and returns it.
      Type Parameters:
      V - the dock view class
      Parameters:
      type - the dock view class
      placement - where to dock it
      Returns:
      the view, once docked
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - while a view is being built, or before the area is created
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null

    • open

      public <F> DockView open(Class<F> factory, Function<? super F, ? extends DockView> create, String key, Placement placement)
      Opens a view created through an assisted factory, as Frames.open(Class<F>, Function) does, and docks it. The views opened through one factory are told apart by key: when one with the same factory and key is open, this brings it to the front, ignores create and placement, and returns it.
      Type Parameters:
      F - the factory class
      Parameters:
      factory - the generated factory class
      create - creates the view with the factory
      key - what tells the views of the factory apart
      placement - where to dock it
      Returns:
      the view, once docked
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - while a view is being built, or before the area is created
      IllegalArgumentException - for a blank key
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null

    • active

      public Observable<Optional<DockView>> active()
      Returns the dock view that has the focus, else the one that had it last, else, when none had it, the one opened last. A view becomes the active one when it is opened, when it is brought to the front, and when a component of its content gains the permanent focus. When the active view closes, the active one is the open view that was active before it most recently, else the one opened last. It changes on the EDT.
      Returns:
      the active view, empty when none is open

    • close

      public boolean close(DockView view)
      Closes a view as an added view is closed: asks the exit vetoes of its scope, and returns false when one vetoes; otherwise undocks it, closes its scope, and returns true. The user closing a view through its header's close button does the same, and nothing when it vetoes.
      Parameters:
      view - the view
      Returns:
      whether it closed
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the view is not open in this dock
      NullPointerException - if view is null
